A former First Mayor of Hamburg and finance minister, this Social Democrat succeeded Angela Merkel as Germany's leader, serving as chancellor from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
Olaf Scholz: Chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025. Olaf Scholz (born 14 June 1958) is a German politician who served as the chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025.

This 19th-century South American conflict was the deadliest interstate struggle in Latin American history, pitting one nation against an allied trio of neighboring countries from 1864 to 1870 — which conflict?
Paraguayan War: Major international war in South America (1864–1870)
A close ally of Robespierre, this French revolutionary chose suicide over arrest when authorities stormed the Hôtel de Ville during the coup of 9–10 Thermidor — who was he?
Born in London to a Ugandan-Indian family, this Conservative MP for Witham served as Home Secretary from 2019 to 2022 before becoming Shadow Foreign Secretary — who is she?
Dubbed 'the greatest living explorer' in 1984, this baronet was the first person to reach both poles by surface travel and later summited Everest at age 65 — who is he?
This British Royal Navy officer reached the South Pole in January 1912, just five weeks after a Norwegian rival — but died with his men on the return journey — who was he?
Robert Falcon Scott: British Antarctic explorer (1868–1912)
The seventh adult man ever to embrace Islam, this military commander led the conquest of a Sasanian capital and founded the garrison city of Kufa — who is he?
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: Muslim general (c. 595 – 674)
Governor of five different Indian states over his career, this politician was serving as the final governor of Jammu and Kashmir when its special status was revoked in 2019 — who is he?
In Hinduism, what name is given to the feminine 'Universal Power' that complements Shiva and is worshipped at shrines called pithas?
Shakti: Divine feminine energy in Hinduism.
Born in 1955, this Princess Royal of Thailand is the second daughter of King Bhumibol Adulyadej and the younger sister of King Vajiralongkorn — who is she?
Sirindhorn: Thai princess (born 1955). Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, The Princess Royal (born 2 April 1955) is a member of the Thai royal family.
In 1956, Britain, France, and Israel jointly invaded Egypt after Nasser nationalized a vital canal — what is this conflict commonly called?
Suez Crisis: 1956 British–French–Israeli invasion of Egypt.
Named to the Time 100 "Heroes" list, this ethologist transformed humane livestock handling and was among the first autistic people to publish insights from her own experience — who is she?
Temple Grandin: American academic and autism activist (born 1947)

Nominated in 2019 by Alexander Gauland to become co-chair of Germany's far-right AfD alongside Alice Weidel, this Bundestag member is known for pro-Russian, eurosceptic foreign-policy views. Who is he?
Led by Gamal Abdel Nasser, this short-lived political union merged Egypt and Syria from 1958 until Syria seceded in 1961, though Egypt kept the name until 1971 — which state?
United Arab Republic: Sovereign state in the Middle East (1958–1971)
Held hostage by the Ottomans as a boy, this three-time Voivode of Wallachia is honored as a Christian hero in Romania for fighting the empire. Who is he?
Vlad the Impaler: 15th-century ruler of Wallachia.

Designed by Irish-born architect James Hoban in the Neoclassical style after a Dublin mansion, this building at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue has been home to every U.S. president since John Adams in 1800 — name this residence?
White House: Residence and workplace of the US president.

After leading an outnumbered army to victory at the Battle of Julu and toppling the Qin, this warlord carved China into Eighteen Kingdoms and founded the short-lived state of Western Chu — who was he?
Xiang Yu: Warload of Western Chu of China (c. 232–202 BC)
As the first Premier of the People's Republic of China, he helped orchestrate Richard Nixon's landmark 1972 visit while also serving as foreign minister during the 1950s — who is he?
Zhou Enlai: Premier of China from 1949 to 1976.
Which of these people was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (born 1851) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Annie Jump Cannon is an astronomer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Ted Kaczynski is a mathematician. The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
What is the atomic number of Palladium?
Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
What is the atomic number of Potassium?
Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
In what year was Sergei Korolev born?
Sergei Korolev: Originally trained as an aircraft designer, Korolev became a leading figure in Soviet rocketry.
In what year was Nostradamus born?
Nostradamus's father's family had originally been Jewish, but had converted to Catholic Christianity a generation before Nostradamus was born.
In what year was Tim Berners-Lee born?
Tim Berners-Lee: Berners-Lee was previously a senior researcher and holder of the 3Com founder's chair at the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL).
In what year did Steve Jobs die?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year did Alan Turing die?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year was Andromeda Galaxy discovered?
Andromeda Galaxy: The Andromeda Galaxy is a barred spiral galaxy and is the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way.
Pillars of Creation: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The astronomers responsible for the photo were Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen from Arizona State University.
Which company manufactures KAI T-50 Golden Eagle?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Korea Aerospace Industries. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
In which country is Convair B-58 Hustler based?
Convair B-58 Hustler: United States. The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight.
Who is credited with discovering Rutherfordium?
Rutherfordium: Albert Ghiorso. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Who is credited with discovering Ampère's force law?
Ampère's force law: André-Marie Ampère. In magnetostatics, Ampère's force law describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two current-carrying wires.
Who is credited with discovering Rhenium?
Rhenium: Walter Noddack. Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.

Despite resembling an unrelated shrub in leaf and flower shape, this shade-loving carrot-family plant has spread worldwide as an invasive garden escapee since being introduced as an ornamental — what is it?
Aegopodium podagraria is a species of flowering plant in the carrot family Apiaceae that grows in shady places.
Endemic to the rainforests of Sumatra, this plant grows an enormous inflorescence that blooms only rarely and briefly, emitting the stench of rotting flesh to lure pollinators — what plant is it?
Amorphophallus titanum is a flowering plant in the family Araceae.
Most often caused by stroke or head trauma, which condition impairs a person's ability to comprehend or formulate language because specific brain regions aren't working?
Aphasia is an impairment in a person's ability to comprehend or formulate language because of dysfunction in specific brain regions.
This gram-positive, spore-forming bacterium was the first ever proven experimentally to cause disease, laying the groundwork for germ theory in 1876 — which microbe?
Bacillus anthracis is a gram-positive and rod-shaped bacterium that causes anthrax, a deadly disease to livestock and, occasionally, to humans.

First flickering to life in octocorals some 540 million years ago and evolving independently at least 94 separate times, this glow is sometimes borrowed from symbiotic bacteria — what is the phenomenon?
Bioluminescence is the production of light by an organism as the result of a chemiluminescence reaction.
This rhythmic bodily process draws oxygen-rich air into the lungs and expels carbon dioxide, powering the cellular chemistry that turns food into energy — what process is it?
Breathing (respiring or ventilating) is the rhythmic process of inhaling air into the lungs providing oxygen, and exhaling the air removing carbon dioxide, in the gas exchange process.
Indigenous to Asia, this genus of flowering plants includes species like sativa, indica, and ruderalis, and is also commonly known as hemp when grown for non-drug purposes — name the genus?
Cannabis is a genus of flowering plants in the family Cannabaceae that is widely accepted as being indigenous to and originating from the continent of Asia.

The only living member of its genus, this big cat sprints at up to 104 km/h thanks to powerful hindlimbs, long legs, and a flexible spine, and wears black tear-like streaks down its face; which animal is it?
Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx.
Mostly belonging to the genus Naja, these venomous snakes are known for rearing upward and flaring a distinctive hood when threatened — name this common snake type?
Cobra is the common name of various venomous snakes, most of which belong to the genus Naja.
Tolerant of poor, sandy soil, this legume was domesticated in Africa millennia ago and is now grown far more in Nigeria and Niger than anywhere else on Earth — which crop?
Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.

First patented in Germany in 1920, then independently synthesized by an American chemist in 1932 and marketed in German-speaking Europe as Permonid for its fast onset and short duration, what is this semi-synthetic opioid?
Desomorphine (or in some formulations known as Krokodil) is a semi-synthetic opioid commercialized by Roche, with powerful, fast-acting effects, such as sedation and analgesia.
Most of the 68 species sharing this name live in Eurasia and Africa, with only two found in North America — and "true" ones are merely a subfamily; what bird is it?
Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.

This genus's tapering spacing of stem nodes toward the tip is credited with inspiring John Napier's work on logarithms; today it's the sole living genus of an ancient, spore-producing plant lineage nicknamed horsetail — which genus?
Equisetum (horsetail) is the only living genus in Equisetaceae, a family of vascular plants that reproduce by spores rather than seeds.

Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed, this slender Mustelid pet weighs up to about two kilograms and comes in coats of black, brown or white — which animal?
Ferret (Mustela furo) is a small, domesticated species belonging to the family Mustelidae.
Caused by a loss of blood supply, this type of tissue death most commonly affects the feet and hands and can turn skin red or black. What condition is it?
Gangrene is a type of tissue death caused by a lack of blood supply. If the gangrene is caused by an infectious agent, it may present with a fever or sepsis.
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and has been called the 'last universal genius' — who is he?
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was German polymath (1646–1716).

One of the first plants ever spun into fiber some 50,000 years ago, which fast-growing Cannabis sativa cultivar is grown for rope, textiles, paper, biofuel and food rather than its psychoactive punch?
Hemp is a plant in the botanical class of Cannabis sativa cultivars grown specifically for industrial and consumable use.
Behaviorally and physically dog-like despite being closer kin to felines, this carnivoran's family is the fifth-smallest in its order with only four extant species — what is it?
Hyena (hi-; from Ancient Greek, haina) are feliform carnivoran mammals belonging to the family Hyaenidae (Latin).
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.
This Liverpool-born mathematician roamed from finite groups to knot theory, but is best loved for inventing a famous cellular automaton called the Game of Life — who was he?
John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 - 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.
Also called the great grey slug, this 10-20cm mollusc has a strange courtship where mating pairs suspend themselves in midair from a mucus thread — what species is it?
Limax maximus (literally, "biggest slug"), known by the common names great grey slug and leopard slug, is a species of slug in the family Limacidae, the keeled slugs.

Resembling some toxic look-alikes despite being a well-regarded edible, this basidiomycete fungus is a fairly common species on well-drained soils across temperate Eurasia, found solitary or in fairy rings in pastures — name the species?
Macrolepiota procera is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
This small southern-African mongoose has digging foreclaws and a knack for thermoregulating in harsh, dry country, living in tight packs of up to 30 — which sharp-eyed animal is it?
Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
Some of these tiny eight-legged arachnids live in soil as decomposers, others on plants causing galls, and one destructive parasite targets honeybee colonies — what are they?
Mite are small arachnids (eight-legged arthropods) of two large orders, the Acariformes and the Parasitiformes, which were historically grouped together in the subclass Acari.
This leafy Brassica rapa crop, native to the area around Beijing, became a widespread vegetable across Europe, the Americas, and Australia in the 1900s — which vegetable?
Napa cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. In much of the world, it is referred to as "Chinese cabbage".
This basic mathematical object is used to count, measure, and label, most commonly represented today through the Hindu-Arabic system of ten symbols — what fundamental concept is it?
Number is a mathematical object used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
This Austrian striker had a brief, injury-hit loan spell at Inter Milan before becoming a regular at Werder Bremen and later playing for a Serbian club. Who is he?
Pan (genus) consists of two extant species: the bonobo and the chimpanzee.
Sprayed on clothing and mosquito nets or applied as a cream against lice and scabies, this pyrethroid discovered in 1972 is highly toxic to fish and to cats — what is it?
Permethrin is a medication and an insecticide.
A large, rounded body that orbits a star but isn't one itself — by the strictest definition, the Solar System has eight of these — what are they called?
Planet is a large, rounded astronomical body that is generally required to be in orbit around a star, stellar remnant, or brown dwarf, and is not one itself.

Caused by a mutation in a single gene that holds the cell nucleus together, this rare disorder makes children age much faster than normal, with most patients living only into their teens or twenties — what's the condition?
Progeria (also Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome or Hutchinson-Gilford progeroid syndrome; HGPS) is a type of progeroid syndrome.

This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species, found worldwide mostly in temperate and mountainous regions, includes a tenacious creeping species common in European gardens as well as bulbous and meadow-dwelling relatives. What are these plants commonly called?
Ranunculus is a large genus of about 1750 species of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Native to West Africa and later naturalized across Asia and the West Indies, this plant's stems yield fibre while its calyces are steeped for a popular infusion — what is it?
Roselle (plant) (Sabdariffa gossypiifolia) is a species of flowering plant in the genus Sabdariffa that is native to Africa, most likely West Africa.
This synthetic element, atomic number 106, is so fleeting that only a few atoms exist at a time and decay within minutes — and it's named for an American nuclear chemist; what is it?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Commonly but inaccurately nicknamed for a big cat it wasn't closely related to, this extinct genus of saber-toothed predator roamed the Americas until as recently as 8,200 years ago — which genus?
Smilodon is a genus of extinct felids. It is one of the best-known saber-toothed predators and prehistoric mammals.
Co-founder of Apple Computer Company in 1976, he also purchased Pixar and returned as CEO in 1997. Who?
Steve Jobs (February 24, 1955 - October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
Modern practitioners prioritize common ancestry as they sort living things into ranked taxa, from domain and kingdom all the way down to species — which biological discipline does this?

Taxonomy (biology) (from Ancient Greek (taxis) 'arrangement' and - (-nomia) 'method') is the scientific study of naming, defining (circumscribing) and classifying groups of biological organisms based on shared characteristics.
Joining Bethesda Game Studios in 1994, this video game director has since led development of both The Elder Scrolls and Fallout series, as well as 2023's Starfield. Who is he?
Todd Howard (born 1970) is an American video game designer, director, and producer who serves as director and executive producer at Bethesda Game Studios.

An oily, amber-colored liquid that's extremely non-volatile and therefore lingers in the environment, this organophosphorus compound was developed for chemical warfare and is lethal in doses of just tens of milligrams — which chemical agent?
VX (nerve agent) is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.

These ear-shaped sea snails wear a shell with a row of breathing holes and a pearly inside, and their flesh is prized as a delicacy worldwide — about 70 species, the biggest a foot long. What are they?
Abalone: Common name for a group of sea snails.
One of the world's few semiaquatic vipers, this venomous pit viper of the southeastern United States coils and displays its fangs when threatened — what is it?
This genus of over 650 succulent species includes a 'true' member long used in pharmaceutical products, native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula — which genus?
Aloe: Genus of succulent flowering plants.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?
One of the oldest of the natural sciences, it leans on math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything from comets to quasars beyond Earth's atmosphere — what field is this?
Astronomy: Scientific study of celestial objects.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.

Having evolved independently at least 94 separate times — first in octocorals some 540 million years ago — this living glow lights up fireflies, deep-sea fish, fungi and dinoflagellates alike; what is it?
Bioluminescence: Emission of light by a living organism.
A synthetic group-7 transition metal made only in particle accelerators, this radioactive element honors a Danish physicist and sits at atomic number 107 — what is it?
Bohrium: Chemical element with atomic number 107 (Bh)

Known also as the Zambezi or Lake Nicaragua species, this aggressive fish can thrive in both salt and fresh water, having been tracked more than 1,100 kilometers up the Mississippi River — what animal is it?
Bull shark: Species of fish. Bull sharks are listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
Sold under the brand name Plavix, this antiplatelet drug taken after a heart attack or coronary stent placement kicks in within two hours and keeps working for five days — what is it?

Clopidogrel: Antiplatelet medication. Clopidogrel, sold under the brand name Plavix among others, is an antiplatelet medication used to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke in those at high risk.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil, plus snackable seeds and birdseed — and its wild cousins sprout multiple flower heads. What is it?
Common sunflower: Species of flowering plant in the family of Asteraceae.
First identified in Europe and interbreeding with Neanderthals as early as roughly 45,000 years ago, this term describes the earliest known modern humans on the continent — what are they called?
Cro-Magnon: Earliest anatomically modern humans in Europe and West Asia.
Nicknamed the 'Radioactive Boy Scout,' this Michigan teenager built a crude neutron source in a backyard shed while chasing his dream of a homemade nuclear reactor — who is he?
David Hahn: American nuclear radiation enthusiast (1976–2016)

This bacterial infection announces itself with a barking, croup-like cough and a tough grey or white "pseudomembrane" that slowly leathers over the throat and chokes the airway — what is this disease?
Diphtheria: Bacterial disease. Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
Nicknamed the spiny anteater, this quill-covered, egg-laying mammal from Australia and New Guinea has babies called puggles — which creature?

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
Named for hindwings that resemble human ears when unfolded, this reddish-brown insect is a common household pest known for the pincers at the tip of its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia: Species of earwig. It is an omnivorous insect belonging to the family Forficulidae.
Nicknamed the 'stomach flu' in the US and Canada, this inflammation of the gut is most often caused in kids by rotavirus and in adults by norovirus — what is it?
Gastroenteritis: Inflammation of the stomach and small intestine.

The only Allied jet aircraft to see combat in World War II, this British fighter entered service with No. 616 Squadron RAF in July 1944, powered by engines pioneered by Frank Whittle — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor: Britain's first jet fighter, 1943–1980s.
This motorsport engineer led the Haas Formula One team from 2016 to 2023 before becoming CEO of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner: Italian and American motor racing engineer (born 1965)
Despite common nicknames like 'Christmas rose' and 'Lenten rose,' this poisonous Eurasian flowering genus isn't actually related to roses at all — what is it?
Discovered in 2013 in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this small-brained archaic human species yielded over 1,500 bone specimens from at least 15 individuals — which species?
Homo naledi: South African archaic human species. The initial discovery comprises 1,550 specimens of bone, representing 737 different skeletal elements, and at least 15 different individuals.
A person with this condition becomes unduly alarmed by even the most minor symptom, convinced a serious illness is upon them despite no medical diagnosis — what is it?
Hypochondriasis: Excessive fear of developing illness.
This cerebrovascular condition is a localized ballooning of a brain blood vessel most often found in the Circle of Willis, with the 'berry'-shaped type being the most common. What is it?

Intracranial aneurysm: Ballooning or rupturing of a blood vessel in the brain. The risk of rupture varies with the size and location of the aneurysm, with those in the posterior circulation being more prone to rupture.
This Swiss psychologist's theory of cognitive development in children gave rise to a field he called genetic epistemology — who was he?

Also called legal theory, this field applies philosophical methods to questions like what the law is and how it ought to be — with roots traced to Confucius, Aristotle, and Enlightenment thinkers like Locke and Rousseau. What field is it?
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.
Nicknamed the sea devil, frogfish, or fishing frog, this species anchors a major commercial fishery in the Irish Sea and ranges from the Barents Sea to the Mediterranean — which fish?
Lophius piscatorius: Species of fish. Lophius piscatorius, commonly known as the angler, toadfish, sea frog, fishing frog, frogfish, or sea devil, is a species of Lophius in the family Lophiidae.
This category of health conditions arises from too few, too many, or an imbalance of nutrients, and can cause anything from stunted growth to obesity. What is it called?
Malnutrition: Medical condition caused by receiving too little or too many nutrients.

Selected in 1969 as a dedicated air-superiority fighter and first flown in 1972, this twin-engine American jet boasts a staggering combat record of 106 victories and zero losses — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle: Multirole and air superiority fighter family.

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.

An Egyptian-born civil engineer and architect who studied in Cairo and Germany, at 33 he was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta: Egyptian terrorist and 9/11 hijacker (1968–2001)
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
This British-American historian, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution, writes on financial history and holds notably favorable views of the British Empire — who is he?
Weighing up to 1,000 kg and resembling a fish head without a tail, this giant marine creature can be as tall as it is long when its fins are extended — what is it?
Ocean sunfish: Species of fish. The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.
This paired female gonad releases egg cells and secretes hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility — which organ?
Ovary: Female reproductive organ that produces egg cells.
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
Native to Eurasia but now introduced worldwide, this game bird has been flagged in the UK as a threat to endangered native adders — what is it?
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Excess fluid pooling in the lungs' air sacs impairs oxygen exchange and can be triggered by either heart failure or a range of unrelated causes — what condition is this?
Pulmonary edema: Fluid accumulation in the tissue and air spaces of the lungs.
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
Slow loris: Genus of primates from Southeast Asia.
